Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

feature noun

a typical or important quality

also characteristic, trait, a feature of, typical of, hallmark, the mark of, typical, that’s typical of him

classical

Cic. Off. 2.17: proprium hoc statuō esse virtūtis, conciliāre animōs hominum
Caes. BG 6.23: hoc proprium virtūtis exīstimant

proprium, propriī n.

noun, second declension (the neuter of proprius); usually proprium est with a genitive

a feature, a characteristic: what belongs to someone or something in particular

Lewis & Short: “a characteristic mark, a sign, characteristic”. The genitive alone can say the same: cujusvīs hominis est errāre, it is in any man’s nature to err (Cic. Phil. 12.5).

Other words

  • habet hoc … ut — has this feature (or advantage), that …

    phrase: habeō with hoc, and an ut-clause saying what the feature is · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 81: habet hoc virtūs … ut virōs fortīs speciēs ejus et pulchritūdō etiam in hoste posita dēlectet

Examples

  • proprium hoc statuō esse virtūtis, conciliāre animōs hominum et ad ūsūs suōs adjungere

    I hold this to be the mark of virtue: to win people’s hearts and attach them to one’s own serviceCic. Off. 2.17

  • Habet hoc virtūs, quam tū nē dē faciē quidem nōstī, ut virōs fortīs speciēs ejus et pulchritūdō etiam in hoste posita dēlectet.

    Virtue, which you do not know even by sight, has this about it: brave men are delighted by its look and beauty even in an enemy.Cic. Pis. 81

  • Cujusvīs hominis est errāre

    Any man may make a mistakeCic. Phil. 12.5

See also features, special, particular, advantage.

SourcesLewis & Short: proprius · Lewis & Short: habeo

Cicero, De officiis 2, In Pisonem and Philippics 12, and Caesar, Bellum Gallicum 6, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
